name: Genève Aéroport

hours.v: open at all times, subject to the night-flight rules
hours.quote: L’aéroport est ouvert en permanence sous réserve des prescriptions applicables aux vols de nuit.

curfew.v: any planned commercial take-off or landing between 22:00 and 06:00 needs the airport operator's prior approval
curfew.quote: tout mouvement commercial planifié entre 22 h et 6 h (atterrissage ou décollage) devra avoir été préalablement soumis à l’approbation de l’exploitant

noise.v: noise quotas apply to the night period 22:00-05:59; for business and general aviation they cover take-offs after 22:00 by aircraft in noise classes IV and V
noise.quote: The available NOISE QUOTAS are determined globally for the night period (10:00 p.m. – 5:59 a.m. LT).

ppr.v: prior permission (PPR) needed for business and general aviation; bookings open 5 days ahead, made through the handling agent
ppr.quote: prior permission (PPR) is required for operations not regulated by Slot Coordination Switzerland.

slots.v: PPR slot booking opens 5 days before the flight; the PPR number goes in item 18 of the flight plan

handling.v: the airport's private aviation contacts list includes TAG Aviation, Jet Aviation, Global Jet, Sparfell and others; separate partner pages for Signature Flight Support, Swissport Executive Aviation and Dassault Aviation Business Services

missing: OSIA art. 39 text itself (fedlex not readable; federal office summary recorded under notable)
notes: Swiss eAIP is a paid product on skybriefing.com and was not read; the federal OSIA text on fedlex could not be opened. The 22:00-06:00 window is the period in which planned commercial movements need prior approval (operating regulations, état 8 Jan 2018 / 1 Jan 2025 versions), not a stated total closure; do not call it a curfew. The handler list is the airport's 'private aviation contacts' list and includes brokers (e.g. LunaJets) that are not handlers; the page also has a 'Show more' button so the list may be incomplete. Partner pages also exist for Signature Flight Support, Swissport Executive Aviation Geneva and Dassault Aviation Business Services (not opened). Do not name companies on the public site (site rule). | 2026-10-27 run: Only new facts for merge. IATA code GVA from the FOCA/BAZL airport page (quote in iata_src). The FOCA SIL object sheet (14 Nov 2018) says operating hours follow OSIA art. 39 ff. but does not give the clock times, and adds that new long-haul flights planned for 22:00-24:00 must use the quietest long-haul aircraft. Fedlex (OSIA text) and the Swiss eAIP (skybriefing, paid) could not be read, so runway, ARP, customs and the exact art. 39 hours stay missing. Slot Coordination Switzerland: GA/BA cannot request airport slots from it at Geneva; all GA/BA flights need mandatory airport movement permission (PPR) via the handling agent (already in the existing file). Facts from the superseded edition other than runway, location and operator were not used (notable). Re-researched 2026-10-29: 29 Oct 2026: The federal environment office (BAFU, page published 18 Nov 2025) states the national night rules: Geneva planned operations to 24:00 plus 30 min for delays, nothing before 06:00 ('Es dürfen aber auch auf den Landesflughägen vor 6 Uhr keine Flugzeuge starten oder landen.' - typo as in source), and non-commercial flights banned 22:00-06:00 ('Starts und Landungen nicht gewerbsmässiger Flüge sind zwischen 22 und 6 Uhr untersagt.'). Read together this means no movements 00:30-06:00 for commercial flights, but no source states that window as such, so the existing curfew (22:00-06:00, approval) was not replaced; consider whether the portal should show 00:30-06:00 as red. Private (non-commercial) flights are banned 22:00-06:00. The FOCA SIL object sheet Genève of 14 Nov 2018 is the only Geneva sheet listed on the FOCA page (checked 29 Oct 2026), so it is the current edition; it gives no runway length. It also says there are no movements 05:00-06:00 ('Il n’y a pas de mouvements durant la dernière heure de la nuit (05h00 à 06h00)'). The operating regulations (état 1 Jan 2025) also name the operator: 'Aéroport International de Genève (AIG), ci-après l'exploitant' and give no runway, customs or size data. Federal customs (BAZG) lists goods offices at Genève-Aéroport, not passenger or aircraft clearance hours, so customs stays missing.
